chapter_title: Concerning the Three Creations of the Flesh: the ones that were brought forth [...]; and the ones that were begotten by the Abortions; and the ones that were formed of themselves.
chapter_note: This chapter is almost entirely a systematic, impersonal teaching sequence classifying animal/plant generation and nourishment within a Manichaean cosmological mechanism (Ambassador, rulers/powers, “thought” descending). Only the brief dialogue-introduction is later hagiographic frame.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame (“Once again our enlightener speaks…”) typical of the Kephalaia’s editorial apparatus; not part of the teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: “All these animals that you see, and also the rest of the [crea]tures [...] of the earth, confirm them in three likeness[es ...]: some from [...] abortions. Others, however, form their own selves in their shape [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal classificatory teaching (threefold typology of generation) with cosmos→cosmos description; no audience exhortation, citation, or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: “Also, their nourishment is thre[e ...] light in them, if they shall wish [...]. [...] they eat see[ds and] fr[uit ...]; they eat seeds and fruit. The [...] it entirely, and they [...] the three archetyp[es] from their nature and the [...] the time when they are on the ea[rth ...]; they are seized [...] in their [...]. The Ambassador [...] all powers [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the mechanistic exposition (nourishment/light; archetypes; cosmic timing), and names the Ambassador as a cosmological agent—internal system explanation rather than later application.

paragraphs.core_text: “[N] it [...], first [...]. Plant them generally to this name: shoots and grass. It formed the bad, bitter trees, the reeds and the thorns and the [...] and these others that are like them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Taxonomic, generative language about plant kinds (“shoots and grass… bad, bitter trees…”) presented as a process within the system; no frame/pastoral overlay. (Page marker removed per extraction rules.)

paragraphs.core_text: “For that thought belongs to the flesh-eating rulers. Still, these [that were] planted (belong to) grass and gourds, since they are in their essence. Nevertheless, [this t]ho[ugh]t that came down from the rulers, as they are in fruit and grass first and shall not be planted in flesh and blood, it formed the trees that shall give nourishing fru[it], as their gourds are sweet.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological causality: a descending “thought” from rulers/powers generating categories of vegetation and fruit; remains entirely within the mythic-cosmic mechanism (no polemical ‘today’, no church address).

paragraphs.core_text: “Again, this thou[ght] that came down from the powers that eat m[ea]t and also eat grass and gourds, it has formed the trees that shall not produce any nourishment. Their fruits belong neither to good nor evil.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Ends the classification by iterating the same internal causal schema (powers → thought → plant outcomes), with a neutral category (“neither to good nor evil”) typical of systematic substrate exposition rather than later moral/pastoral use.
